issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, but the solution introduces a FeedResponse type and declares Animal.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. This diverges from the exercise specification and adds an extra class (FeedResponse) not mentioned in the problem. Students following the problem statement will implement messageOnFeed() to return String, while the solution's API requires FeedResponse, creating confusion and potential test/compilation mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Either revert the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and remove FeedResponse), updating Seal/Pig/Goat to return String; or update the problem statement and UML to specify FeedResponse as the return type and document the FeedResponse class. Prefer the first option to match the exercise specification: remove FeedResponse and use String consistently.

issues.description: Within the solution repository there is an internal inconsistency: Animal.messageOnFeed() is declared to return FeedResponse, and Seal and Pig implement it returning FeedResponse, but Goat.messageOnFeed() is implemented to return String. This mismatch will cause compilation errors in the reference solution and is structurally inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the reference implementation so all Animal subclasses use the same return type. Either change Goat.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse (consistent with Animal) or change Animal and the other subclasses to use String. Ensure the solution compiles and matches the method signature declared in Animal.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an abstract method messageOnFeed() that returns a String (Animal.messageOnFeed(): String). The solution implementation changes this contract: Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse object and a new FeedResponse class is introduced. This creates a naming/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (an animal's feed message) across artifacts. Students reading the problem/template expect to implement and use messageOnFeed() as a String and will be confused by the solution returning a FeedResponse type and by the presence of a FeedResponse class that is not mentioned in the task description or template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnFeed() contract consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution so Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String (and have Pig/Seal/Goat return their feed message Strings), removing or repurposing FeedResponse; or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly specify and document the FeedResponse return type and the FeedResponse class structure so students are aware that messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse rather than a String.
